coverage.reason: Defines the actor classes; supplies no narrower category of classified licensed firms.
Names STREAMS 2 and describes its replacement of STREAMS and intended benefits.
Submission heading.
Establishes the mandatory channel and introduces the permitted methods; read with launch timing and footnote 2.
XML option carries footnote 3.
Completed prescribed PDF option carries footnote 3.
Web-form option has no footnote 3 marker.
Registration heading.
Recommends account registration and directs new users to email the registration form; this email instruction does not authorize ordinary STR filing by email.
Transitional-arrangements heading.
Uses should for observing transitional arrangements; does not erase the express mandatory wording of the XML provision.
Defines cessation and resumption times and the blackout interval.
Direct-contact instruction attaches to urgent submission during the blackout; contact alone is not established as completed filing.
Establishes launch and discontinuation timing; migration, record access and applicable consent-status access are distinct from resubmission.
Requires XML schema conformity and prompt liaison to arrange a technical test. The selected filing control evaluates conformity only; the separate preparatory obligation remains unevaluated.
General query contact, not an alternative STR filing channel.
Issuing division.
Issuing institution.
Document end marker.
Document identifier.
Footnote 1 supplies webinar background; November introduction dates do not replace February launch timing.
First fragment of the external presentation URL; presentation contents are not supplied.
Remaining fragment of the external presentation URL; adds no supplied substantive requirement.
Identifies footnote 2 associated with the exclusive-channel sentence.
Adds mandatory resubmission after a qualifying other-channel submission and announces facilitating guidance; neither authorizes that channel nor expressly suspends the obligation pending guidance.
Identifies footnote 3, whose markers appear on XML and PDF options.
Requires Hongkong Post e-Cert for the marked XML and PDF options; operational satisfaction remains unresolved.

dimensions.explanation: The selected control concerns one actual post-launch STR filing by a licensed firm. Resubmission and urgent blackout contact are separate controls. No whole-firm compliance determination follows.
Licensed firms comprises the three stated classes. Classified describes an assessment of membership, not a separate source-defined class. Filing, contact and migration must remain distinct.

Footnote 2 adds a remedial resubmission duty rather than permission to use another channel. The blackout instruction attaches only to urgent submissions during that interval. Footnote 3 attaches to XML and PDF, with no supplied basis to extend it to the web form.

Required establishes mandatory channel, XML and resubmission provisions. Should and please govern registration and blackout contact. Will provide guidance is descriptive and supplies no express condition precedent.

The proposed operational boundary is 9:00am on 2 February 2026, following the blackout starting at midnight on 28 January. Equating implementation with operational launch is an explicit assumption; timezone and resubmission deadline are unspecified.

All three footnotes are supplied, resolving piece-local absence claims. XML schema, prescribed PDF specification, operational e-Cert requirements and resubmission guidance remain unavailable. The four opaque missing dependency identifiers cannot be mapped from this packet.

questions: Does implementation in footnote 2 mean the operational launch at 9:00am on 2 February 2026, and what timezone governs?
What operational evidence establishes satisfaction of the Hongkong Post e-Cert requirement, beyond merely possessing or having access to a certificate?
What requirements do the separate XML schema and prescribed PDF specification impose?
What procedures, deadlines and blackout follow-up obligations does JFIU resubmission guidance prescribe?

assumptions: The selected event is assessed separately from any later resubmission.
Licensed-firm classification uses the three source-defined classes without an additional narrower classification.
The operational launch bounds the post-launch control; the rule is not applied during the blackout.
Footnote 3 attaches to both marked methods, XML and PDF.
Unknown facts remain unknown. Certificate satisfaction requires an external assessment grounded in operational requirements; possession alone is insufficient evidence.
The formula is conditional on externally supplied technical assessments and excludes registration, technical-test liaison, STR timeliness and whole-firm compliance.

citations.quote: licensed corporations, SFC-licensed virtual asset service providers and associated entities (collectively referred to as “licensed firms”)
Licensed firms are required to submit STRs to the JFIU via STREAMS 2 by one of the following means:
submission of an STR in an Extensible Markup Language (XML) format3;
uploading a completed STR form in the prescribed PDF format3; or
completing the web-based STR form in STREAMS 2.
upon the launch of STREAMS 2 at 9:00am on 2 February 2026
are required to follow the XML schema provided separately by the JFIU
Hongkong Post e-Cert (electronic certificate) is required for this submission.
For STRs submitted to the JFIU via channels other than STREAMS 2 following its implementation, licensed firms are required to re-submit the STRs via STREAMS 2.

readings.distinction: Retains the parent's channel-and-method reading while repairing its unresolved is_xml_submission reference. Footnote 2 attaches a further duty to an off-channel filing; it does not make that original filing compliant if later resubmitted. The competing hypothesis that footnote 2 permits alternative initial channels fails because its text requires resubmission without granting permission or retrospective cure. Extending footnote 3 to the web form likewise lacks an anchor. The strongest remaining uncertainty is the operational meaning of satisfying the certificate requirement.

assumptions: Following implementation is interpreted as at or after operational launch.
The result concerns the selected submission event, not the complete submission history of an STR.
Unknown facts remain unknown; contact is not assumed to be filing.
No deadline, discharge condition or permission to file off-channel is inferred.

citations.quote: For STRs submitted to the JFIU via channels other than STREAMS 2 following its implementation, licensed firms are required to re-submit the STRs via STREAMS 2.
The JFIU will provide guidance to facilitate the re-submission.
upon the launch of STREAMS 2 at 9:00am on 2 February 2026

readings.distinction: This complementary reading makes footnote 2's attachment explicit as a separate event-level trigger. An off-channel post-launch filing can fail the initial channel control and trigger mandatory resubmission simultaneously. A false result for this event does not exclude a qualifying event elsewhere in the same report's history. Implementation's precise boundary remains the strongest textual uncertainty.

readings.subject: Event-level trigger for mandatory resubmission

assumptions: The blackout begins at 12:00am on 28 January 2026 and ends when submissions resume at 9:00am on 2 February 2026.
The urgent-contact direction retains its please wording under the transitional should provision.
Pre-launch blackout contact is not treated as a post-implementation filing.

citations.quote: Licensed firms should observe the JFIU’s transitional arrangements as set out below:
the JFIU will cease accepting STR submissions via STREAMS at 12:00am on 28 January 2026, and will resume accepting STR submissions at 9:00am on 2 February 2026 via STREAMS 2
for any STRs requiring urgent submission during the blackout period of STREAMS, please contact the JFIU directly by email (jfiu@police.gov.hk), phone at 2866 3366 or fax at 2529 4013;

readings.distinction: The blackout arrangement attaches to urgency during a bounded interval, not to urgency at any time. It therefore does not supply a continuing post-launch exception. A hypothesis that every listed contact method completes filing or automatically triggers footnote 2 lacks support. The source does not settle follow-up for blackout-only submissions.
questions: What constitutes completed urgent filing through the blackout arrangements, and what later follow-up is required?
readings.statement: For an STR requiring urgent submission during the blackout, licensed firms are directed to contact JFIU through a listed email, phone or fax method. This instruction remains separate from the post-launch channel control and does not establish that contact alone completes filing.
readings.subject: Urgent blackout contact and its limited attachment
